publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: In recent years, significant progress has been achieved in medical image segmentation by leveraging deep neural networks based on the U-Net architecture and skip connections. While widely used in medical image segmentation, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have limitations in learning global semantic information due to their localized convolutional operations. Additionally, fusion methods like element-wise addition or concatenation in encoder-decoder architectures often introduce unnecessary information, leading to the loss of local details. To address these challenges, we introduce FusNet, an innovative information fusion network. FusNet combines features from Swin Transformer and Res2Net, enhancing global dependency relationships and low-level spatial details. A fundamental subtraction unit (DIV) is used to eliminate redundant information in each layer, reducing high-level up-sampling-induced redundancy. Finally, FusNet aggregates features from various layers to produce segmentation results in the decoder. Evaluation on four diverse medical image datasets, including polyps, eye diseases, cell nuclei, and breast cancer, demonstrates FusNet's remarkable segmentation performance and robustness, surpassing alternative methods. FusNet holds significant potential for improving medical image segmentation tasks. The source code of FusNet is freely available at https://github.com/HaoWuLab-Bioinformatics/FusNet

articleTitle: CAHAN: Drug-Disease Association Prediction Based on Cross-Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: In order to obtain high-quality node embeddings, a drug-disease association prediction model CAHAN based on cross-attention mechanism is proposed in this paper. After obtaining drug and disease node representations through graph neural networks using a hierarchical attention mechanism, the interactions between drugs and diseases are learned using a cross-attention mechanism, and link prediction is subsequently performed. We compare the performance of proposed model CAHAN with some state-of-the-art models. The experimental results show that the proposed model CAHAN exhibits significant improvements over those previous methods and achieves satisfactory performance, which validates the effectiveness of the model CAHAN. In order to obtain reliable negative samples, a negative sampling strategy based on drug similarity is proposed in this paper, in which the similarity between drugs is evaluated by introducing additional target information, and then the scores of drug-disease pairs are calculated to obtain reliable negative samples. Experiments are conducted on all models, and experimental results show that the performance of all models is significantly improved after applying the proposed negative sampling strategy compared with random negative sampling, which verifies the feasibility of the proposed drug similarity-based negative sampling strategy. And a case study is designed to validate the biological interpretability of CAHAN.

articleTitle: Prompting Meta-Learned Hierarchical Graph Network for Molecular Property Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: In the realm of molecular research, the observation of molecular properties often comes with a limited number of molecular samples. Consequently, researchers have framed the task of molecular property prediction as a few-shot problem. Existing methods for few-shot molecular learning treat molecules as graphs where atoms serve as nodes and bonds serve as edges. However, these approaches commonly overlook the inherent significance of functional groups, also known as motifs. Moreover, it is crucial to recognize that diverse molecular properties may exhibit intricate associations with different motifs. When predicting properties in new tasks, it becomes imperative to adaptively focus on the relevant motifs. To tackle this limitation, we investigate prompting a meta-learned hierarchical graph neural network (HGNN). The HGNN extracts motifs from the original molecular graph and obtains two distinct views of the molecule: the lower atom-level and the higher motif-level. Then it employs a cascading message passing paradigm to propagate information from atoms to motifs within the molecule. To enable the HGNN to adapt quickly to new tasks with rarely supported samples, we propose to learn a novel task prompt in meta-learning. The task prompt fills the gaps between tasks by discerning and assigning higher importance to the motifs that are specifically relevant to each task. Specifically, the task prompt is learned from a comprehensive task context, which incorporates two types of information: textual semantic features and class prototypes. Extensive experimental results on four benchmarks show the superior performance of our method. Our code is available at https://github.com/HICAI-ZJU/PH-Mol.

articleTitle: MED-INPAINT: Medical Image Synthesis Using Multi-Level Conditional Inpainting with a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model and Adaptive Contrast Priors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) have shown promise for generating high-resolution synthetic images. In medical imaging, there is a growing demand for both realistic image synthesis and deterministic outcomes that can guide downstream applications effectively. In this study, we propose MED-INPAINT, an adaptable multi-level conditional DDPM framework. MED-INPAINT incorporates contrast priors for accelerated sampling and performs inpainting of pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans, enabling high-quality image synthesis with reasonably low uncertainty. Our results highlight the effectiveness of MED-INPAINT in generating realistic and detailed pelvic MRI images, assessing its uncertainty using various denoising steps at inference. MED-INPAINT outperformed baseline U-Net and cycle-consistent generative adversarial network (Cycle-GAN) models, demonstrating its potential for various medical imaging applications.

articleTitle: Subnetwork Mining Based on Structure Entropy for Analyzing Depression Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The exponential growth in protein-protein interaction network provides lots of opportunities and challenges to identify un-annotated essential proteins and reveal functional modules associated with depression. Mining associated subnetworks is an effective method to explore depression from a system-level, since it can reduce the size of network and make network analysis feasible and more focused. In this paper, we propose a subnetwork mining method to extract disease associated subnetworks by minimizing structure entropy that highlights the influence of key proteins and functional modules on the disease in question. Based on protein-protein interaction network and known key proteins, our approach initiates by constructing an initial subnetwork induced by a set of known key proteins. Subsequently, we partition this subnetwork into distinct modules using a structure entropy minimization algorithm. Each of these modules within the subnetwork can be considered a potential protein complex, allowing us to uncover their functional implications. Finally, we selectively extract a set of proteins by minimizing structure entropy, thereby ensuring the acquisition of relatively complete modules that better represent the functional aspects of the system. To reduce computational cost, we explore the relationship between the increase of structure entropy and the variance of the edge number sequence, which comprises the counts of edges connecting newly added nodes to existing modules. As a result, we transform the task from minimizing structure entropy to the more tractable problem of maximizing the variance of the edge number sequence. This approach optimizes our computational efficiency while retaining the effectiveness of our method. We evaluate the approach on tasks related to depression. Based on the extracted subnetwork, our model exhibited strong performance in predicting essential proteins across 9 centrality measurements. We selected 23 newly discovered proteins with degree centrality values exceeding 0.2 for enrichment analysis, the enriched pathways primarily pertained to stress-activated MAPK cascade, positive regulation of DNA-binding transcription factor activity, and regulation of inflammatory response etc., which highly related to depression. We also evaluate biological significance of functional modules on obtained subnetwork. The KEGG pathway enrichment analysis reveal that the six modules with the highest number of associated pathways, which relating to signaling pathways, neurodegenerative diseases and nervous system, among others. Furthermore, KEGG pathway enrichment analysis conducted on the predicted proteins and functional modules underscored the rationality and validity of our algorithm. This approach provides a fresh perspective for exploring the pathological mechanisms underlying depression.

articleTitle: scGAT: A Cell-Type Annotation Framework for Single-Cell Transcriptomics Using Graph Attention Network and Meta Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has emerged as a valuable tool for classifying cell types across various species, tissues, and environmental conditions, thereby advancing the field of life sciences. Automatic cell annotation plays a crucial role in bioinformatics, addressing the challenges associated with time-consuming and labor-intensive manual cell annotation. Although numerous cell annotation algorithms exist, their performance is often constrained by the quality of reference data and inherent technical noise in biological experiments. To address these challenges, we propose the integration of a heterogeneous graph neural network into our cell annotation model, named scGAT. This integration leverages the intricate relationships between expressed genes and cells while disregarding unexpressed genes. Additionally, we introduce a novel approach that utilizes prototype cells to mitigate technical noise. However, the use of prototype cells may lead to limitations in sample size, prompting us to employ meta-learning techniques to determine the model's initial parameters. To assess the effectiveness of scGAT in cell annotation tasks, we conducted comparative analyses using real datasets against other models. The experimental results clearly demonstrate that scGAT significantly outperforms alternative methods.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Sleep and Anxiety States of an Individual with Anxiety Disorder by Utilizing Deep Neural Networks and Heart Rate Variability Based on Fingertip Pulse
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Anxiety disorder is a prevalent psychological condition that can impact individuals' blood pressure and sleep patterns. This study employs a photoplethysmographic sensor to gather fingertip pulse data from a patient with an anxiety disorder over the course of one year. Both heart rate variability and deep learning methodologies are utilized to investigate the inherent correlations between the patient's anxiety levels, sleep quality, and blood pressure. A total of 824 five-minute samples of fingertip pulse data are utilized, and the data is categorized based on sleep quality and anxiety levels. After preprocessing steps such as noise reduction, both time-domain and frequency-domain heart rate variability indices are calculated. The analysis is carried out across various categories, illustrating that heart rate variability can effectively discern physiological states based on fingertip pulse data. Finally, the EfficientNetB0 neural network is employed to predict blood pressure values, and trends in blood pressure during different anxiety and sleep states are analyzed. The results indicate that blood pressure varies across different sleep and anxiety states. This research provides a non-invasive method for understanding individuals with anxiety disorders' sleep issues and anxiety states, offering valuable insights for clinical treatment and intervention.

abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in medicine and healthcare has a long history. With the rapid development in AI, especially deep learning and most recently generative models, the huge transformative potential of AI to medicine, healthcare, and the society, has again gained a renewed interest. At the same time, risks and damages caused by inadequate application of AI technologies, such as bias, data and information security, transparency and trust, are high on the agenda too.
